title: Fra Giovanni di Lucca to Ferdinand III, 30 May 1644 (DECODE R2159, ÖStA HHStA Staatskanzlei Interiora, Chiffrenschlüssel Kt. 20 Fasc. 27 ff. 18-19)

plaintext.source: Tomokiyo gave only 'Al principe di trenti...'; DECODE lists it non-decrypted.

transcription.notes: Tomokiyo's transcription; checked on the DECODE images 22 Sept 2026 (ten 17 -> 14) and 14 Nov 2026 (group 79 is 21, not 32).

system.summary: 23-figure Italian alphabet in dot-delimited 1-2 digit groups, a few homophones; no polyphony (17 and 19 were misreadings or encipherment slips: 17 = i, 19 = s).
system.doubled_letters: written once (one doubled pair in 231 groups)
system.notes: i has 15 and shares 17 with n; s only through 19.

prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo's unsolved page: opening 'Al principe di trenti...' only

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Unconstrained homophonic annealing, 16 restarts; converges on a non-Italian optimum.
Tomokiyo's crib 'Al principe di' taken literally needs 17 = i and n.
Eight consistent crib letters fixed, other 16 figures annealed; all six seeds agree on Italian.
Polyphony 17 = i/n, 19 = t/s read off the contexts.
Same procedure on five shufflings scores -3.40 to -3.68 per 5-gram against -2.50.
Viterbi over the alternatives reads all 231 groups; two spots ambiguous.
DECODE R2159 images P1-P2 fetched with the account cookie (first session had only Tomokiyo's transcription).
Cipher checked group by group against f. 18r: the writer's crossed 4 was transcribed as 17 in ten groups (principe x2, mandero, con, una, non x2, vinto); corrected to 14.
With the corrections 17 = i only; Viterbi changes only Bogodanna->Bogodania and no il habi->non l'habi. Clear frame names Koniecpolski as the speaker, dated Brody 30 May 1644.

Polyphony withdrawn after G. Lasry's review: 19 is s (six times, s has no other figure); the three places needing t are encipherment slips (19 in both places of Transiuania on the image). Key table and page corrected.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 231 tokens, 24 types, it-cinquecento order 4: reading -2.043 per letter; random keys -4.124 (z 8.1); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.865 (mean -2.922, z 18.0); annealer on the real text -2.75. Verdict: pass.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): ct.txt (corrected transcription) and plaintext.txt (decryption) linked; corrected key table copied from docs/lucca.html to texts/key.md.
Read bar applied per document (v10): 1 of 1 documents marked read measure under 95% of words read as sense (v2_score explicit holes) and are now read in part; read_share recorded for each.

Brice Dudout (Claude Opus 5.5): cipher of f. 18r re-read on the DECODE R2159 images (P1, full resolution): 230 of 231 groups as in ct.txt; group 79 (rivoltare) is 21, not 32, so figure 32 goes (23 figures; letter r unchanged). The nine 19s come in two shapes (plain 1, dotted 1) that do not follow the value: the three places wanting t have the plain form, as do four of the six s. Independent decoder (verify_dudout_20261114.py) reading only texts/key.md and ct.txt: 226 of 231 letters as in plaintext.txt; key unchanged. The brackets of plaintext.txt mark the cipher u of Transiuania and the cipher o of Bogodania (both on the page), while the supplied l, the supplied i of ogni and the three 19 = t emendations are unmarked or silent; checked on the image. A diplomatic text with {+x}/{-x} markers reproduces all 231 cipher letters: 52 of 56 words read from the key as written (0.929), 4 with forced emendations, 0 unresolved; v2_score 1.0. Class not changed. VERIFY_dudout_20261114.md.

outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt by annealing with eight letters fixed from Tomokiyo's published partial decipherment 'Al principe di trenti...' (cryptiana variable2.htm), found before the attempt; the clear frame of the letter was not seen until the second session.
outcome.notes: Transcription corrected against the DECODE images 22 Sept 2026 (ten 17->14); 17 is not polyphonic; 19 = s, its three t-contexts are the writer's encipherment slips (G. Lasry, 21 Sept 2026: no polyphony here). Odd spellings ogn, Transiuania look like the writer's. Speaker Koniecpolski per the clear frame.

texts.label: R2159, 30 May 1644, f. 18r cipher paragraph
texts.summary: Fra Giovanni di Lucca, writing from Brody, relays to the Emperor an offer from Grand Hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski: he will by every means stop the Turk from helping the Prince of Transylvania (György Rákóczi I, who had invaded Habsburg Hungary in February 1644), will if need be set the Prince of Moldavia against him with two thousand Cossacks, and asks that the Emperor make no peace until Rákóczi is humbled or defeated.
texts.note: 24 Oct 2026: 94.6% of the words of plaintext.txt read as sense (v2_score explicit holes); coherent sentences but under the 95% read bar, so read in part.
